content:
Anna Roberts: paging — seeing KV cache pressure and runaway continuous-batch sizes on rope-serving pool after long-context rollout (NTK ~65k). p99 token latency spiking; some nodes hitting OOM thresholds. :rotating_light:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered (SEV=P1) — metrics: kv_cache_evictions ↑, batch_size_avg ↑, batch_latency_p99 ↑. Linked monitors: #KV-Cache, #Rope-Serving, #ContinuousBatching.
Sam Patel: I'm jumping on logs and tracing. Which region / pool?
Anna Roberts: eu-west-1 rope-pool-yarn. YaRN + sliding-window flag enabled in last canary at 11:42 UTC.
Maria Gomez: tagging support to surface customers. @SupportBot can you check error rates / customer-facing slowdowns?
SupportBot: ACME and FTL-Search reported timeouts and degraded responsiveness starting ~11:50 UTC. Estimated impacted requests: ~1800 reqs over 12m, many retries. No 500s confirmed; mostly timeouts and 30s+ tail latency.
Sam Patel: pulling node-level metrics: continuous_batch.size_avg climbed from 6 -> 240 in 6m for some workers, KV cache creating huge prefix entries for rope longctx windows. Looks like sliding-window + high NTK clients created enormous KV caches per-request.
Lee Chen: if batch size growth is uncontrolled it multiplies KV cache writes and eviction churn. We need an immediate throttle on continuous batching and evict problematic prefixes.
Jason Liu: propose hotfix: 1) cap continuous-batching max-size to 16 on rope pool, 2) evict KV cache entries with prefix rope/longctx/*, 3) rollback sliding-window flag for YaRN canary.
Evan Brooks: agree. I can run the commands. Are we ok with brief latency bump from capping?
Anna Roberts: yes, prefer predictable higher latency than OOMs / timeouts.
Sam Patel: steps to run now — will coordinate:
```
# cap continuous batching immediately
ropectl set-batching --pool rope-pool-yarn --max-batch-size 16 --continuous true
# evict suspect KV entries
kvctl evict --prefix "rope/longctx/" --region eu-west-1 --confirm
# rollback canary flag
deployctl rollback-flag --name yarn_sliding_window --env canary
```
Maria Gomez: please post the commands you run and timestamps so SRE can correlate.
Evan Brooks: executing ropectl cap (running now). ETA 20s.
DeployBot: Command queued: ropectl set-batching --pool rope-pool-yarn --max-batch-size 16 --continuous true — started by Evan Brooks.
Evan Brooks: cap applied on rope-pool-yarn. confirmation: all nodes report max_batch_size=16.
Sam Patel: evicting KV prefixes now. Running kvctl command.
infra-bot: kvctl evict started: 3 worker tasks; estimated 2m.
Sam Patel: evict completed. Approx 48k keys removed; eviction throughput ~800/s.
Jason Liu: rolling back sliding-window flag on canary.
DeployBot: rollback-flag yarn_sliding_window (canary) started by Jason Liu.
Jason Liu: rollback complete for canary. Will keep staging + prod paused.
Maria Gomez: Support — any change in customer reports post-mitigation?
SupportBot: ACME says response times improved within 2 minutes of interventions; follow-up tickets opened for both accounts. No data loss reported.
Anna Roberts: monitoring — batch_size_avg back to ~8, kv_evictions trending down, node memory stable. p99 latency falling but still above normal for some slices (12s -> now ~2.1s).
Sam Patel: running additional sanity checks: KV cache hit rate normalized, rope-inflight token counts returned to steady state.
Evan Brooks: left a light-touch throttle in config to prevent immediate regrowth: continuous-batching backoff multiplier set to 0.5 when batch_size > 32.
Lee Chen: good. Also added temporary adaptive eviction for rope/longctx prefixes to cap per-request KV writes.
Anna Roberts: handing off to Sam for stabilization and postmortem. I'm going offline in 10. Sam, escalate to infra if any memory anomalies reappear.
Sam Patel: taking over on-call. I'll watch metrics for 60m and collect flamegraphs and heap profiles if needed.
Jason Liu: preliminary customer-impact summary: ~2 enterprise customers experienced timeouts and high tail latency for ~10–18 minutes; no requests lost but retries increased. Recommend outreach + credits per incident policy.
Maria Gomez: opening postmortem ticket and adding runbook updates to prevent sliding-window + high-NTK clients from creating per-request KV explosion.
Anna Roberts: next steps: 1) postmortem, 2) add safety caps in runtime (hard cap on KV keys per request), 3) refine canary gating for longctx features to include kv_eviction rate, 4) add automated rollback trigger if continuous_batch.size > 128 for >2m.
Sam Patel: I'll attach logs and timestamps. Closing pager when metrics hold for 60m.
IncidentBot: Incident state changed -> mitigated. Assigned: Sam Patel.
Evan Brooks: thanks all. :thumbsup:
Anna Roberts: good job team. We'll do a formal postmortem tomorrow.
SupportBot: Notifying affected customers and creating follow-up tickets.
Sam Patel: last check at 18:00 UTC — system stable. Marking last_message_ts.
